label: reasoning-distillation-research-complete
context:
Researched reasoning distillation for Qwen3.6-35B on DGX Spark. KEY FINDING: structure of long CoT matters MORE than content correctness (Li et al 2025). Corrupting step content drops accuracy 3-4%, but corrupting structure drops 12-14%. This means: (1) don't need perfect teacher traces, (2) structural patterns of reflection/backtracking/self-verification are what transfer, (3) just 17K examples via LoRA produced 15.2% avg accuracy improvement (Bespoke-Stratos matched o1-preview).

DATASETS RANKED:
1. OpenThoughts2-1M (1M examples, 8.3GB, best coverage)
2. OpenR1-Math-220k (220K, math-focused, DeepSeek-R1 traces)  
3. Bespoke-Stratos-17k (17K, proven LoRA baseline, $800 to generate)
4. NuminaMath-CoT (73K, competition math with step-by-step)
5. CodeContests (13K, code reasoning with explanations)
6. MedQA-CoT (~12.8K + custom generation from GLM-5.1)

LORA CONFIG FOR REASONING (different from behavioral):
- Rank 64-128 (NOT 16 — reasoning needs higher rank)
- Alpha 128-256
- LR 1e-4 to 3e-4 (higher than behavioral)
- Sequence length 8192 (reasoning traces are long)
- Targets: q/k/v/o/gate/up/down_proj (more modules than behavioral)

DATA MIX: Math 30-35%, Code 15-20%, STEM 15-20%, Medical 10-15%, Qwen-native 10-15%, Self-generated 5-10%

PHASES:
1. Bespoke-Stratos-17k baseline (1 week, +10-15%)
2. OpenR1-Math + NuminaMath + GLM-5.1 medical traces (2-3 weeks, +15-25%)
3. OpenThoughts2-1M (month 2)
4. Ongoing domain specialization + self-play loop
